transcript.text: I need to share what I found during my billing review this afternoon. I reconciled the provider quote with the last six months of artifact-retrieval data, and the numbers don't match the draft plan's assumption. Archive storage would actually cost 7,800 USD per month once retrieval fees are included — not 4,000 USD. Standard object storage, on the other hand, comes in at exactly 5,400 USD per month, which stays under our approved 6,000 USD monthly cap. I haven't posted the corrected model yet, but I wanted everyone to have these figures before we discuss the plan.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share something critical before we go further. This morning, while testing an unrelated CI plugin, I confirmed that exactly 37 of the 100 CI pipeline artifact paths depend on POSIX rename semantics that archive object storage cannot provide. The remaining 63 pipelines can migrate to object storage without issue. I haven't updated the migration ticket yet, but this directly affects which pipelines we can move and should factor into any plan we approve today.

transcript.text: I need to share my compliance findings before we proceed. This morning I confirmed with the audit team that release artifacts for regulated products must be retained in immutable storage for exactly 730 days. The current draft plan's 90-day deletion policy and unlocked object storage do not satisfy that requirement. I had not opened the compliance finding yet, but it directly impacts what we can approve today.
